records.title: An Introduction to Causal Inference
records.version: IJ Biostatistics6(2)Article7(2010); author-hosted corrected reprintR-354 datedMarch2011
records.nature: author-hosted corrected published-paper reprint selected body, not a whole-paper audit
records.read_scope: §2.1 PDFp3 lines64–91; §3.2.1 and Definition2 PDFp11–13 lines350–413; §4/4.1 PDFp27 lines913–936; §4.3 PDFp29–30 lines991–1028

propositions.supported: Associations alone do not identify intervention effects. Identification is relative to causal assumptions and the target query; equal observational distributions must imply equal target values within that assumed model class. Defining, identifying and estimating a query are separate tasks.
propositions.limitations: The two-model enumeration illustrates Definition 2 under explicit finite assumptions. Actual causal studies require their own model, estimand and identification argument.
